narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 66.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That does not mean failure is certain; it means that, based on the academic profile submitted, the risk was considered too high for admission at this time.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the first decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. This difference pushed the prediction strongly toward bar-exam failure. The second most influential factor was your first-year class standing: you were in the fourth decile, below the accepted-student average of about the sixth decile, and this also pushed toward failure. Your law school admission test score was the third most important factor. At 36 it was only slightly below the accepted-student average of 37.18, and in this case it contributed in the direction of passing rather than failing, but it was not enough to offset the weaker class-standing signals.

To improve a future application, focus on strengthening the academic indicators the review relied on: seek advising about your third-year performance, consider whether retaking the admission test is realistic, and document any circumstances or upward trends. Ask admissions for feedback, and consider additional coursework or legal experience before reapplying if the program permits.
